title: Luring the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Out of a Cave with Music; Death of the Fire God
medium: Hanging scroll, ink and color on paper
subject: Amaterasu, Iwato (heavenly rock-cave), Ame-no-Uzume
description: The kami perform music and dance at the cave mouth to lure the Sun Goddess Amaterasu back out after her retreat into the Iwato, which plunged the world into darkness. A celebrated Edo-period depiction of the Iwato myth.
attribution: Metropolitan Museum of Art (Met Open Access, public domain)

title: Amaterasu Emerging from the Cave (Origin of the Iwato Kagura)
subject: Amaterasu, Iwato, kagura dance
description: Kunisada's large print of Amaterasu emerging from the rock-cave — the moment that gave rise to the Iwato-kagura ritual dances performed at shrines to this day.

title: Amaterasu Appearing from the Cave
subject: Amaterasu
description: The leading Meiji-era printmaker Yoshitoshi depicts the Sun Goddess emerging from the cave of heaven.

title: Amaterasu
subject: Amaterasu
description: A Meiji-period image of the Sun Goddess, part of the 19th-century revival of Shinto imagery.

title: Amaterasu (from a shinbutsu-zue, 'illustrated compendium of deities')
subject: Amaterasu
description: From the famous 1790 shinbutsu-zue, an early mass-produced illustrated catalogue of Japanese kami — an important witness to Edo-period popular kami imagery.

title: Susanoo-no-Mikoto Slays Yamata-no-Orochi in Izumo
subject: Susanoo, Yamata-no-Orochi, Izumo
description: The iconic scene: Susanoo strikes the serpent's final head after luring it with sake in the barrels along the river.

key: File:Dragon Susanoo no mikoto and the water dragon.jpg
title: Dragon: Susanoo-no-Mikoto and the Water Dragon
subject: Susanoo, Yamata-no-Orochi
description: Kuniyoshi's dramatic Edo-period treatment of Susanoo's battle with the great serpent.

key: File:Susanoo rescues Kushinada Hime by Toyohara Chikanobu 1886.jpg
title: Susanoo Rescues Kushinada-hime
subject: Susanoo, Kushinada-hime
description: Chikanobu's late-Meiji print of the moment Susanoo finds the weeping Kushinada-hime, daughter of the earth deity, whose story he is about to hear.

key: File:Izanami and Izanagi create the 1st Japanese isles, Kobayashi Eitaku MFA 1880s.jpg
title: Izanagi and Izanami Creating the First Japanese Islands
subject: Izanagi, Izanami, creation of the islands
description: The creator pair stand on the bridge of heaven, stirring the brine of the sea with the jeweled spear Ame-no-nuhokohe to form the islands.

title: The God Izanagi and Goddess Izanami
subject: Izanagi, Izanami
description: A monumental early-20th-century image of the divine creator pair by one of the leading painters of the period.
attribution: Metropolitan Museum of Art (Met Open Access, public domain)

title: Izanagi and Izanami (from a shinbutsu-zue)
subject: Izanagi, Izanami
description: The creator pair as depicted in the 1790 illustrated compendium of deities — one of the earliest widely circulated images of the pair.
